newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ABN AMRO downgrades Zalakeramia to "hold".
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO downgrades Zalakeramia to "hold".

text.p: ABN AMRO Hoare Govett downgraded Hungarian tile manufacturer Zalakeramia Rt to "hold" from "buy" after the company's results in the first quarter were below the securities house's expectations.
"Q1 results were below our expectations," Tommy Erdei, Budapest-based analyst at ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett said in a desknote. "Pricing pressures continued and exports fell heavily."
Zalakeramia reported an IAS net profit of 144.2 million forints for the first three months of 1997 against a net profit of 105.4 million in the same period of 1996.

The analyst said that Zalakeramia's recent capital increase of 1.04 billion forints from 1.836 billion has diluted earnings per share (EPS) forecast, which is 358 forints for 1997 and 455 forints for 1998. These EPS forecasts exclude the recent acquisitions of Inker in Croatia and Pietra in Hungary.
"The newly acquired companies will likely remain loss-making in 1997 and most of 1998, reducing EPS further," Erdei added.
